title: Microsoft Lands in Crosshairs of New U.S. Crackdown - TradingView
content: Microsoft MSFT is facing a new U.S. immigration-related constraint after the government suspended the company from using the PERM labor-certification program, potentially making it harder to convert some foreign workers into permanent U.S. residents. The move adds a new workforce risk for Microsoft and several other technology companies already navigating tighter immigration scrutiny. Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that Microsoft had abused the immigration system by laying off U.S. workers while continuing to benefit from large numbers of work visas and green cards. "Unfortunately, no one has abused this program more than Microsoft," Vance said. He cited roughly 6,000 Microsoft layoffs last year alongside 6,300 new visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. "Thanks to an ongoing investigation, we have decided to suspend the PERM program for Microsoft, which means they will no longer be able to take those H-1Bs and apply for permanent resident status within the United States of America," Vance said. PERM is the labor-certification process employers generally use before sponsoring many foreign workers for employment-based green cards. Losing access does not shut off H-1B hiring entirely, but it can complicate the longer-term retention of affected workers. Other companies reportedly suspended from PERM include Cognizant CTSH, Infosys INFY, Wipro WIT, Adobe ADBE, HCL and Capgemini. Wipro and Infosys shares fell more than 3% after the announcement, while Cognizant declined roughly 2%. Microsoft shares were little changed. The administration also announced investigations into alleged J-1 visa abuse involving several major U.S. universities. For Microsoft, the immediate financial effect is likely limited, but the strategic risk is meaningful if immigration restrictions begin constraining access to specialized engineering and AI talent. Investors should watch whether the suspension is temporary, whether Microsoft challenges it, and whether similar restrictions expand to other visa programs. The bigger concern is sector-wide. If immigration rules become materially tighter, technology companies could face higher labor costs, slower hiring and greater competition for U.S.-based technical workers. For now, the issue looks more like a talent-acquisition and compliance risk than a direct earnings shock. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services. Select reference data provided by FactSet. title: Michael Burry Raises Red Flag Over Popular Big Tech Stock - TradingView
content: Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) is taking aim at Microsoft's MSFT massive AI infrastructure spending, arguing that the company may be using its financial scale as a lever to get what it wants rather than responding purely to unavoidable demand. The criticism goes beyond Microsoft, raising a broader investor question over whether hyperscalers are spending rationally or racing to secure dominant positions before the AI market consolidates. Burry's argument centers on the unprecedented capital spending underway across Microsoft, Amazon AMZN, Alphabet GOOGL, Meta Platforms META, Oracle ORCL, OpenAI and Anthropic. He argues that dominant technology companies should not need to spend as aggressively as if their core businesses were under existential threat. The only reason the CEOs of these tech monopolies are spending wildly on data centers like they are is because they assume they will be granted an oligopoly that is too big to fail, Burry said. He has separately argued that major technology companies, excluding Apple AAPL, are spending as if their lives depended on it when their lives clearly do not. Burry extends the thesis to newer AI players as well. No, but they intend to be part of the oligopoly. None can imagine breaking the dominance of a Microsoft, Amazon AMZN, Google GOOG, or Meta META within each silo. The implication is that today's AI spending race may partly reflect a strategic land grab: securing compute, data-center capacity and customer ecosystems before rivals can establish durable advantages. For Microsoft investors, the critical issue is whether enormous AI capital expenditures generate returns that justify the spending. Investors should watch Azure growth, AI-related revenue, capex intensity, free-cash-flow conversion and depreciation expense. If cloud and AI revenue continue scaling faster than infrastructure costs, Burry's criticism weakens. The risk grows if spending remains elevated while utilization, pricing or customer monetization disappoint. The broader market implication is significant because many of the largest U.S. technology companies are following similar strategies. If returns on AI infrastructure fall short, investors may eventually question not just one company's capex plan, but the valuation framework supporting the entire hyperscaler spending boom. title: MSFT, ORCL, NVDA, QQQ In Focus: OpenAI’s Annualized Revenue Reportedly Trails Prior Expectations By $20B - Stocktwits
content: OpenAI’s annualized revenue is about $20 billion lower than previously indicated, financial documents provided to investors reveal, potentially cooling exuberance around the pace of artificial intelligence demand, according to a Financial Times report. In recent communications with investors, the artificial intelligence research and deployment company said its annualized revenue approached $50 billion at the end of September. The figure falls well short of the $70 billion estimate widely reported late last month based on data initially supplied to investors, the Financial Times reported. Annualized revenue serves as a primary metric for gauging market adoption across the generative AI sector. Financial analysts closely track the benchmark for both OpenAI and key competitor Anthropic to justify surging public equity valuations and sprawling tech infrastructure expenditures. Most AI-linked stocks, including Microsoft (MSFT), a key OpenAI investor, Oracle (ORCL), Nvidia (NVDA), Broadcom (AVGO), Intel (INTC), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Cerebras (CBRS), eased on the lower-than-expected annualized revenue. The iShares semiconductor ETF (SOXX) and the VanEck semiconductor ETF (SMH) eased between 2% and 3% on Thursday. OpenAI investors sought to standardize revenue performance against Anthropic, a person familiar with the matter told the Financial Times. The two AI developers use different accounting methods to calculate annualized performance. Anthropic includes revenue generated from cloud platform distribution partners, including Amazon Web Services (AWS) (AMZN) and Google Cloud (GOOG, GOOGL). Conversely, OpenAI excludes sales made through third-party cloud channels from its core calculations. Attempts to "gross up" OpenAI's figures to match Anthropic's reporting structure led to initial estimates that OpenAI had reached $40 billion in annualized revenue in August, according to the Financial Times. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits related to OpenAI was ‘neutral’ with ‘normal’ message volumes. One user highlighted the effect of the lower annualized revenue on the wider tech space. Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) shares drew significant investor attention on Thursday after Starbucks reportedly explored a potential takeover of the restaurant chain. The Financial Times reported that a purchase of Chipotle, with a market value of nearly $41 billion, would be the largest tie-up in the restaurant sector in history. CMG shares were up about 6% at the time of writing on Thursday, while SBUX shares were down about 3%. According to the report, Starbucks has worked with advisers in recent months on a potential takeover proposal for Chipotle. The status of the plans, including whether Starbucks has submitted a formal offer, remains unclear. People familiar with the matter told FT that a transaction of this size may not ultimately move forward. If completed, the transaction would surpass Burger King's $11.4 billion acquisition of Tim Hortons in 2014, making it the largest restaurant acquisition on record, according to FT. The potential combination would bring together two large U.S.-focused restaurant businesses. Starbucks operates about 41,000 owned and licensed stores globally, with roughly two-fifths located in the U.S., while Chipotle has about 4,200 restaurants, almost all in the U.S. Together, the companies generated nearly $50 billion in sales last year, based on their respective reported figures. The potential transaction would also involve Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol, who previously led Chipotle for more than six years. Niccol left Chipotle in August 2024 to become Starbucks' chief executive. At Starbucks, Niccol has been overseeing the company's 'Back to Starbucks' strategy, which includes adding baristas, introducing new menu items, speeding up service and renovating cafes. Starbucks has also hired former Chipotle executives Tressie Lieberman and Stephen Piacentini to lead marketing and coffee shop development, respectively, according to the FT. Chipotle recently appointed Sabir Sami, the former CEO of KFC, to its board, effective immediately. The company said Sami brings more than 30 years of global consumer and restaurant-industry experience, including 16 years at Yum! Brands. Separately, Chipotle is expanding its restaurant leadership pipeline as it works toward a long-term goal of 7,000 restaurants across the U.S. and Canada. The company expects to open 350 to 370 new restaurants in 2026 and aims to have an Apprentice in every restaurant by the end of 2027. More than 85% of Chipotle's restaurant managers began their careers as Crew Members, the company said. Shares of Immunovant (IMVT) sold off Thursday as traders treated Argenx’s (ARGX) failed late-stage Sjögren’s trial as a warning for its own experimental drug for the autoimmune disorder. Immunovant (IMVT) fell about 6% to $30.06 in morning trading. Its parent Roivant (ROIV) was also weaker, trading down roughly 2%. Immunovant is developing IMVT-1402 in an ongoing mid-stage study in Sjögren’s disease. Argenx’s efgartigimod works the same way: it lowers circulating IgG antibodies that can drive autoimmune disease. A late-stage failure for a closely related drug raises the odds that simply reducing IgG may not be enough in Sjögren’s. The move also follows Immunovant’s late-September setback, when IMVT-1402 missed its main goal in a cutaneous lupus study, and that program was dropped. Roivant is the majority owner of Immunovant, and IMVT-1402 is central to the group’s autoimmune story. Argenx has stopped its late-stage UNITY study of weekly subcutaneous efgartigimod in adults with moderate-to-severe Sjögren’s disease. An independent monitoring committee, after an interim look, said the trial was unlikely to meet its main goal: a reduction in systemic disease activity at week 48, the company said. Safety matched the drug’s known profile, with no new signals. Sjögren’s, which causes dry eyes, dry mouth, fatigue and joint pain, still has no approved targeted therapy and is unusually varied from patient to patient, which makes trials hard to win. Argenx’s U.S. shares were down about 14% to $797.69. The drug is already approved as Vyvgart for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP). The failed trial removes the Sjögren’s path for Vyvgart. H.C. Wainwright analyst Douglas Tsao called it a good-news, bad-news day for Argenx. On the positive side, the analyst said a 126-patient mid-stage study of FB102 in celiac disease met its primary endpoint. Argenx acquired FB102 through its $2.2 billion acquisition of Forte Biosciences. The firm sees that result as real validation of Argenx’s Forte deal and a clear step toward a late-stage study. The UNITY stop, by contrast, was a “surprising setback,” the firm said. Wainwright said it is now more cautious about what the failure implies for Immunovant’s mid-stage Sjögren’s study of IMVT-1402. It kept a ‘Buy’ on Argenx and a $1,202 price target. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around IMVT and ROIV was in 'neutral' and 'bearish' territory, respectively. Sentiment around ARGX, however, jumped from 'bearish' to 'bullish' territory. IMVT stock has gained 19% this year, while ROIV has gained 55%. ARGX, however, has lost 4%. Editas Medicine (EDIT) was on investors’ radar on Thursday after Australian authorities cleared the biotech firm’s experimental gene-editing treatment for its first human clinical trial, prompting Wells Fargo to upgrade the stock. EDIT shares gained around 4.7% before paring most of the gains. On Thursday, Editas said it received approval to begin the Phase 1/2 Strive trial of EDIT-401 in Australia. The treatment targets heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, an inherited condition that causes unusually high levels of LDL, or bad cholesterol, increasing the risk of heart attacks and strokes. The company said EDIT-401 is designed to edit the LDLR gene, helping remove bad cholesterol from the blood after a single treatment. Existing cholesterol medicines require repeated doses. In studies on non-human primates, the drug reduced bad cholesterol and other harmful blood fats by around 90%, with cholesterol reductions maintained for 10 months. Editas plans to begin patient dosing this year, report initial safety data in the first quarter (Q1) of 2027, and topline safety and efficacy data later in the year. Following the update, Wells Fargo raised its rating on the stock to 'Overweight' from 'Equal Weight' and hiked its price target to $6 from $4, according to The Fly. This represents a 114% upside potential from current levels. EDIT has a 12-month consensus price target of $5.9, with eight of the 13 analysts covering the stock having rated it a ‘Buy,’ three ‘Hold,’ and two ‘Sell,’ according to Fiscal.ai Wells Fargo believes starting the trial marks an important step toward proving EDIT-401’s potential as a differentiated cholesterol treatment. The firm sees 2027 as a possible turning point for Editas’ valuation if early results show meaningful cholesterol reductions. While EDIT-401 is the company’s lead development program, Editas is also pursuing gene-editing treatments for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, two inherited blood disorders, as well as a cancer-cell therapy collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb. The company reported $211.6 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, following a $125 million financing in May. Editas expects its existing funds to support operations into the second half of 2028. title: Microsoft's Visa Freeze Could Trigger an AI 'Brain Drain' - TradingView
content: The Donald Trump administration suspended Microsoft Corp. MSFT and Adobe Inc. ADBE from the Department of Labor’s Permanent Labor Certification, or PERM, program, which companies use to sponsor eligible foreign workers for permanent U.S. residency, reported Reuters. The action also covers Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp CTSH, Infosys Ltd. INFY, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro Ltd. WIT, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. The action does not directly affect current H-1B visa holders. Instead, it blocks a common route for skilled foreign workers to transition to permanent residency, potentially making the U.S. a less certain destination for talent companies want to retain. Read Also:  What's Going On With Microsoft Stock Thursday? Todd Warren, founding partner at Envorso, said H-1B limits can be “quite negative for companies” and push them to look offshore. “Capping H1B’s in effect creates a ‘brain drain’ of people who have been educated in the U.S.—as these people leave and go back to their home countries instead of adding to the U.S. workforce and capacity,” Warren warned. Warren noted that developer demand has already fallen significantly from its 2022 peak as Big Tech shifts spending from human capital toward data centers and AI infrastructure. That could cushion the immediate impact, but it does little to resolve the longer-term talent question. Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management, similarly said the immediate financial impact on major technology companies is likely limited, while the implications for innovation and competitiveness could be much larger. Mahoney pointed to Nvidia Corp. NVDA CEO Jensen Huang and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD CEO Lisa Su as examples of immigrant leadership in semiconductors. If restrictions broaden or become permanent, Mahoney said companies could face higher hiring costs and stronger incentives to shift research and development overseas. The White House has also extended restrictions on certain H-1B workers through September 2027, with covered petitions generally subject to a $100,000 payment, subject to exceptions. For Microsoft, Nvidia and Broadcom Inc. AVGO, the immediate question is not whether they can hire another developer. It is whether the U.S. remains the easiest place to assemble the world’s best AI researchers, engineers and founders. Investment Takeaway: Investors should watch hiring costs, overseas R&D expansion and management commentary on talent availability. The bigger risk may not appear in next quarter’s earnings, but years later in where America’s next AI breakthroughs are built.  is anchoring the technology tape on Thursday as the cloud-and-artificial-intelligence heavyweight draws steady attention while major indexes ease from record highs set earlier in the week. The pullback has been driven by climbing bond yields and oil pushing back toward the hundred-dollar mark, and the software giant has navigated it with less turbulence than many of the high-flying chip and memory names. Artificial intelligence and semiconductors remain the dominant theme in the market, and Microsoft sits at the intersection of both. It runs one of the largest cloud platforms in the world, it has a deep partnership with a leading model developer, and it embeds generative features across productivity software that hundreds of millions of workers use daily. That breadth is why the stock often serves as a bellwether for enterprise technology spending. In sessions like this one, when some corners of the market are swinging sharply, a company with diversified revenue, a fortress balance sheet and recurring subscription streams tends to attract attention as a stabilizer. Microsoft fits that description, even as it spends enormous sums on data centers to keep pace with demand. This article walks through what is keeping Microsoft in focus, how its major businesses interact with the current backdrop, and what market participants are watching in the period ahead. It is a descriptive review of the situation and not a call on direction. The broader market has paused for breath after reaching fresh peaks. Bond yields have climbed, raising the bar for companies whose earnings are weighted toward the period ahead. Oil near the hundred-dollar mark has revived concerns about inflation and consumer budgets, while gold trading near record highs reflects a measure of caution among some traders. Within that setting, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite both retreated from record levels, though the declines have been orderly. Bank earnings are about to open, and the results from large lenders will provide a read on credit conditions, corporate borrowing and consumer health, all of which feed into technology demand. For Microsoft, higher yields cut two ways. They can weigh on how the market discounts long-dated cash flows, but the company's cash generation is large and predictable, which cushions the effect. They also raise the cost of capital for customers, and enterprise buyers sometimes slow large projects when financing grows pricier. Energy costs matter at the margin as well. Data centers are power-hungry, and the price of electricity and fuel influences the cost of running them. The cloud platform known as Azure is the principal growth engine within Microsoft. It supplies computing, storage, databases and a growing menu of artificial intelligence services to businesses of every size, and it competes head to head with the largest rivals in the industry. Growth in the segment has been strong for years, and the market watches each quarterly update for signs of acceleration or fatigue. Demand has been fueled by two forces. The first is the ongoing migration of workloads from private data centers to the cloud, a multi-year shift that still has room to run. The second is the surge of interest in training and running artificial intelligence models, which requires massive amounts of specialized computing capacity. Beyond the cloud, Microsoft owns some of the most entrenched software in the world. Office applications, Windows, Teams, Dynamics business tools and the developer platform GitHub touch nearly every corner of the modern workplace. The recurring nature of those subscriptions produces stable revenue and gives the company a built-in distribution channel for new features. The company has been layering a family of assistants known as Copilot across that portfolio. Copilot can draft documents, summarize meetings, write code and analyze spreadsheets, and it is offered as a paid add-on for business customers. The commercial success of this strategy is one of the most closely watched questions in technology. A defining feature of the Microsoft story is its long-running alliance with a leading artificial intelligence lab. The relationship gave the company early access to cutting-edge models, which it integrated into search, productivity tools and its cloud offering, and it helped reposition Microsoft as a leader in the generative era after years of being seen as a follower. The arrangement has evolved. The lab has pursued additional infrastructure partners and a more independent corporate structure, while Microsoft has broadened its own model efforts and added alternatives to its platform. The shift reflects the maturing of the market, where no single supplier is expected to dominate every use case. Few topics generate more discussion than the scale of Microsoft's capital expenditures. The company is constructing data centers at a breakneck pace, buying vast quantities of graphics processors and building out power and cooling systems. The spending runs into the tens of billions of dollars each year, and it is rising. The justification is straightforward. If artificial intelligence usage continues to expand, capacity shortages will cap growth, and rivals will capture demand that Microsoft cannot serve. Underbuilding is seen as more dangerous than overbuilding, at least while customers are lining up for capacity. Several items will shape how Microsoft trades in the coming weeks. Bank earnings are on the near horizon, offering clues about corporate and consumer health. Inflation readings and central bank commentary will influence expectations for interest rates, which matter greatly for large growth-oriented technology names. On the company front, the market will look to supplier updates, data center announcements and any news on Copilot adoption or new model launches. The next quarterly report will be scrutinized for cloud growth, capital spending guidance and commentary on capacity constraints. Product events and developer conferences can also supply headlines. title: Is Microsoft Stock a Buy After Expanding Its Nvidia Partnership? - TradingView
content: Microsoft MSFT) is strengthening its position in artificial intelligence after expanding its collaboration with Nvidia NVDA) and introducing a new generation of AI-powered Windows PCs. On Wednesday, Microsoft unveiled pricing and availability details for its Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by Nvidia's RTX Spark chip, which enables developers and consumers to run AI models directly on their devices rather than relying entirely on cloud infrastructure. Starting at $2,599, the new laptop will become available on October 16, alongside Nvidia-powered AI PCs from Dell DELL), HP HPQ), Lenovo LNVGY), and other manufacturers. Additionally, Microsoft announced the Nvidia-powered Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, designed for developers and AI engineers working with advanced models, which is expected to ship in November at a starting price of $5,999. The collaboration could help Microsoft capture additional demand for AI-enabled computing while strengthening its Windows and Surface ecosystems. Microsoft's growth trajectory remains encouraging, supported by expanding demand for Azure cloud services, enterprise AI applications, and its Microsoft 365 Copilot offerings. During its most recent fiscal fourth quarter, Microsoft reported revenue of $90 billion, up 18% year over year, while adjusted earnings climbed 23% to $4.74 per share. Looking ahead, the Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for Microsoft's current fiscal 2027 revenue to climb 17% to $390.2 billion, with earnings expected to increase 9% to $19.65 per share. Furthermore, FY28 sales and EPS are each projected to rise another 18%, highlighting the company's favorable longer-term growth prospects. Although Microsoft’s growth outlook remains strong, earnings estimate revisions have been largely unchanged. The FY27 EPS consensus is slightly up in the past 60 days from $19.63 to $19.65, while FY28 estimates have dipped from $23.30 to $23.24. This suggests analysts remain confident in Microsoft's growth outlook but have yet to become more bullish on its near-term earnings trajectory. At current levels, Microsoft stock trades at 27X forward earnings, well above its Zacks Computer-Software industry's average of 16X and at a slight premium to the benchmark S&P 500. This premium reflects Microsoft's leadership in cloud computing, recurring enterprise software revenue, and expanding AI opportunities. Still, elevated expectations leave shares vulnerable to volatility if Azure growth slows or the company's substantial AI infrastructure investments pressure profitability. Microsoft's expanded Nvidia collaboration adds another catalyst to its compelling long-term AI growth story. However, MSFT shares are up a respectable but relatively modest 9% year to date, suggesting investors may be gravitating toward other high-growth opportunities with stronger near-term momentum. Combined with its premium P/E valuation and relatively stagnant earnings estimate revisions, Microsoft stock currently lands a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), with MSFT being more appealing as a long-term holding than an aggressive near-term buy. content: Microsoft MSFT changed how it reports its business in September 2026, and the change puts its AI investment case in sharper focus. Starting with fiscal 2027, the company has merged its three reporting segments into two: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer. The new Agents and Infra segment groups Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud and industry solutions together. Restated figures show the segment generated $268.1 billion in revenues and $136.4 billion in operating income in fiscal 2026, which works out to an operating margin above 50% even at the peak of the buildout. Management expects first-quarter fiscal 2027 Agents and Infra revenues of $75.15-$75.75 billion. The spending is enormous. Fiscal fourth-quarter capital expenditures were $41 billion, and roughly two-thirds of that went to short-lived assets, mainly CPUs and GPUs. First-quarter capex is expected to exceed $50 billion, and a lease reclassification has lifted the calendar 2026 estimate to about $175 billion. Free cash flow fell to $19.6 billion from about $25.6 billion a year earlier, and Microsoft Cloud gross margin fell year over year to 65%. The strongest offset is how much future demand is already visible. Commercial remaining performance obligation jumped 84% to $678 billion, and about 30% of it is expected to be recognized as revenue within 12 months. Azure revenues exceeded $100 billion for the first time in fiscal 2026. Under the new definition, Azure is projected to grow 44-45% in constant currency in the first quarter, while Microsoft 365 commercial cloud is expected to grow about 17%. That outlook is supported by more than 30 million paid Copilot seats and new usage-based billing. For fiscal 2027, Microsoft expects double-digit growth in revenues and operating income. It sees full-year operating margins slipping by less than a point and free cash flow staying positive. Because so much of the spending goes to short-lived hardware, the company can slow purchases quickly if demand weakens. Rising depreciation and margin pressure remain real risks. Even so, guidance anchored in a large contracted backlog suggests the capex cycle is increasingly backed by committed demand. How Amazon and Alphabet Stack Up on AI Capex Returns Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOGL are pursuing similarly aggressive AI infrastructure buildouts. Amazon raised its 2026 cash capex outlook to about $220 billion. AWS revenues climbed 37% to $42.2 billion in the second quarter, and its backlog reached $496 billion. Amazon expects capacity to remain short of demand into 2027. Alphabet lifted its 2026 capex guidance to $195-$205 billion, as Google Cloud revenues surged 82% to $24.8 billion. Alphabet's cloud backlog stood at $514 billion, with slightly more than half expected to convert into revenue within 24 months. However, Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative in the second quarter. Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra in San Francisco as it pushes deeper into AI-powered personal computers and takes aim at Apple’s MacBook Pro. The new laptop is built around Nvidia’s RTX Spark superchip, which combines a central processing unit with Blackwell graphics technology and up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory for running AI models locally. Microsoft is pairing the hardware with new Windows 11 features designed for what it calls hybrid intelligence, combining local AI processing with cloud computing for larger workloads. The company also introduced Execution Containers, a security system designed to isolate AI agents and limit their access to data and other resources, as Microsoft seeks to address concerns about autonomous software operating on personal computers. Chief executive Satya Nadella and Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang appeared at the San Francisco event alongside Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft’s Windows and Devices chief, highlighting the partnership behind the new hardware platform. (MSFT) is doubling down on AI-powered Windows PCs as it looks to challenge Apple Inc.’s (AAPL) Mac lineup, unveiling a broader push to bring powerful AI models directly onto devices. Microsoft also started preorders for its Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) RTX Spark Arm-based chip and priced at $2,599. Shipments begin on Oct. 16. Microsoft said the machine can run AI models with more than 120 billion parameters locally, with configurations offering up to 128GB of unified memory. Microsoft shares rose 0.1% on Wednesday, its fourth consecutive session of gains, but dipped marginally in overnight trading. Microsoft said it is bringing local versions of models including DeepSeek V4 Flash, its own MAI Code 1.1 Flash and Nvidia’s upcoming Nemotron to Windows. MAI Code 1.1 Flash, for example, has been compressed substantially to run locally, while DeepSeek V4 Flash is a 284-billion-parameter model that Microsoft says can run on RTX Spark systems. Microsoft is also preparing a native Meta Muse app for Windows. Meta launched a native Muse app for Mac on Sept. 17. Microsoft shared details about the upcoming “Hybrid Intelligence” features that let Copilot use files on a Windows PC to take actions and a new search experience that allows users to do quick actions from the search bar. “There will never be a moment where we say, ‘this runs locally, this runs in the cloud.’ Hybrid intelligence will be everywhere,” CEO Satya Nadella said onstage at the company’s Windows and Surface-focused event in San Francisco. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who joined Nadella onstage, framed RTX Spark as a fundamental shift in personal computing. “This is the only computer on the planet that runs everything natively on the device — DirectX, OpenGL and every CUDA application,” Huang said, arguing that the platform combines capabilities historically spread across PCs and cloud. Nvidia unveiled the RTX Spark platform earlier this year as a new class of Windows processors, built for local AI agents, combining a Blackwell RTX GPU with a 20-core Grace CPU. content: Microsoft (MSFT) share price jumped 2% on Monday to its highest level in over nine months as it prepares a push in its AI silicon strategy by boosting production ahead of the release of the Maia 300 chip. According to a report by The Information, the tech giant is seeking to drastically scale up its in-house hardware capabilities to counter rising infrastructure costs and diminish its heavy dependence on Nvidia Corp (NVDA). To support the rollout, Microsoft has been negotiating with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) to secure capacity for more than 300,000 Maia 300 units targeted for delivery in 2027. The source noted that Microsoft's ultimate goal is to obtain production capacity for over 1 million units, though supply constraints for key components and ongoing capacity negotiations with TSMC could affect total volume. The projected production target marks a steep increase from the tens of thousands of Maia 200 chips produced to date. Past efforts encountered delays after early tests failed to hit internal performance targets. As a result, deployment of the current Maia 200 line has remained limited to just two data centers located in the U.S. In a statement to The Information regarding the production targets, Andrew Wall, Microsoft’s general manager for Azure Maia, declined to confirm specific volume figures but emphasized the long-term vision. "We expect our Azure Maia deployments to support AI workload demand measured in gigawatts," Wall stated, pointing to infrastructure scale that would eventually require millions of AI processors. CEO Satya Nadella has long aimed to reduce the software company's reliance on Nvidia's dominant market position. Unsealed court documents from a 2022 internal email revealed Nadella lamenting that Microsoft was "a very thin layer on top of Nvidia" while absorbing high operating expenses to host AI models. The economic rationale for the transition is central to Microsoft's strategy. Microsoft informed investors last month that running OpenAI and internal AI models on Maia 200 processors reduces operational costs by 30% to 40% compared to top-of-the-line Nvidia hardware. Microsoft currently lags behind hyperscale peers such as Amazon.com Inc. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google in third-party adoption of custom hardware. Google plans to manufacture over 3 million Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) this year, while Amazon's Trainium processors have secured large-scale commitments from major developers, including Anthropic. Shares of Tenax Therapeutics (TENX) crashed nearly 89% to a record low in early trading on Monday, after the biotech firm’s experimental drug TNX-103 failed to meet the main goal of a late-stage study in patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, or PH-HFpEF. PH-HFpEF is a condition in which pressure in the blood vessels of the lungs increases while the heart has difficulty filling properly. The Phase 3 LEVEL trial enrolled 241 patients and evaluated whether TNX-103, an oral form of Levosimendan, could improve how far patients could walk in six minutes after 12 weeks of treatment. Patients receiving TNX-103 improved their six-minute walk distance by 14 meters, compared with 10.4 meters for placebo. The 3.5-meter difference was not statistically significant, meaning the study did not show convincing evidence that the improvement was caused by the drug. TNX-103 also failed to significantly improve a key questionnaire measuring heart failure symptoms. However, the trial also showed that patients who could initially walk less than 333 meters improved by 26.3 meters compared with placebo. TNX-103 also produced a 49% greater reduction in NT-proBNP, a biomarker that rises when the heart is under stress, compared with placebo. The drug also reduced right ventricular systolic pressure, a measure of pressure on the right side of the heart, by 3.5 millimeters of mercury compared with placebo. Tenax said TNX-103 was generally well tolerated with no new safety signals. Tenax said it plans to meet with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to discuss the full results and potentially adjust future trials to focus on patients who showed a stronger response to TNX-103. The company will also seek guidance from European regulators. “We believe the data from LEVEL provide new information that will guide us toward approval. MoonLake Immunotherapeutics (MLTX) was in the spotlight in pre-market trading on Monday, after the biotech firm reported positive topline results from a Phase 3 trial of its psoriatic arthritis treatment, along with a narrower -than-expected second-quarter loss. MoonLake’s Phase 3 IZAR-1 trial tested Sonelokimab in adults with active psoriatic arthritis who had not previously received biologic treatments. The study met all clinical endpoints at Week 16 for the 60 mg dose with induction. The trial’s primary endpoint was ACR50, which measures whether patients achieve at least a 50% improvement in signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis. At week 16, 42.1% of patients treated with Sonelokimab achieved that response. The drug showed improvements across other measures. About 66.5% of patients achieved ACR20, while 41.2% reached minimal disease activity. On Wednesday, Microsoft held a Surface product launch event, unveiling the price and release schedule for the new flagship laptop, the Surface Laptop Ultra, which is powered by an NVIDIA chip, and claiming that its performance on certain artificial intelligence (AI) tasks surpasses that of comparable Apple products. Zhitong Finance APP learned that Microsoft (MSFT.US) held a Surface new-product launch event on Wednesday, unveiling the price and release schedule for the new flagship laptop, the Surface Laptop Ultra, which is powered by NVIDIA (NVDA.US) chips, and claiming that its performance in certain artificial intelligence (AI) tasks outperforms comparable products from Apple (AAPL.US). According to Microsoft executives on Wednesday, the Surface Laptop Ultra can process prompts up to twice as fast as Apple's MacBook Pro M5 when running local AI models, and generate videos up to six times faster than comparable Apple devices. The Surface Laptop Ultra is now available for pre-order and will begin shipping on October 16; its starting price is $2,599, about $400 less than the entry-level 16-inch MacBook Pro. This brand-new Surface device is built on an NVIDIA chip designed for Windows laptops. The chip will support both general-purpose computing and AI computing. This also opens up a new competitive arena for NVIDIA against mainstream PC processor manufacturers such as Intel (INTC.US) and AMD (AMD.US). NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang took the stage alongside Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella to discuss the development of this brand-new PC chip. Huang stated, "We've completely reinvented the personal computer." Other PC manufacturers that use the Windows operating system, such as Dell Technologies (DELL.US) and HP Inc (HPQ.US), have also developed devices equipped with this new NVIDIA chip. This is not the first time Microsoft has sought to leverage the AI boom to boost device sales. In the summer of 2024, Microsoft, together with partners including Qualcomm (QCOM.US), launched a large-scale marketing campaign targeting AI‑optimized PCs. At the time, Microsoft pledged that these devices would embed AI capabilities directly into the hardware, achieved by adopting more powerful chips based on designs from Arm Holdings (ARM.US). However, the launch of this product line was hampered by privacy concerns raised over one of its flagship features, which was originally intended to provide users with a useful record of their device usage. In recent years, as Apple desktop computers have seen a surge in demand thanks to their outstanding performance in running AI models, Microsoft is striving to maintain the Windows operating system's dominant position in the AI era. According to estimates from research firms, despite Windows being the most popular PC operating system, the company does not rank among the world's top six PC vendors in terms of shipments. With advances in AI and chip technology, tech giants including Microsoft, Apple, and Google (GOOGL.US) are working to enable users to run more AI workloads locally on their devices rather than relying on the cloud. Nadella stated that over time, developers and users will expect AI tools to be powered by both local hardware and cloud services. In addition, during the event, Microsoft executives outlined the advantages of using Windows for AI-related tasks. Developers can leverage the computing power of new devices without paying cloud service providers, thereby reducing costs and enhancing security. They also highlighted Windows' security features, which can be used to monitor and control the behavior of AI agents. The company further stated that Meta (META.US) will launch a Windows version of its popular Muse AI agent, capitalizing on the surging popularity of this personal assistant—which has surpassed ChatGPT to top the Apple App Store rankings. title: Dan Ives Thinks AI Buildout Still In Early Stages, With NVDA, MSFT, PLTR, AAPL And CRWD As Top AI Picks - TradingView
content: The global shift toward artificial intelligence is still in its infancy, and market investors continue to underestimate the magnitude of an impending multi-trillion-dollar expenditure cycle, tech industry analyst Dan Ives told CNBC. Initiating coverage across nearly 50 technology firms, Ives outlined an extremely optimistic outlook for the sector. Ives emphasized that despite geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic headwinds, and ongoing regulatory debates, the market is misjudging the scale of an incoming $4 trillion spending wave. "We believe this is the 3rd inning of a 9-inning game, and the scale of what is now committed is the evidence," Ives said in an interview with CNBC, noting that secondary and tertiary market opportunities from AI adoption are only beginning to unfold across the corporate landscape. Ives identified chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT) as primary infrastructure beneficiaries. He assigned an "outperform" rating and a $300 price target to Nvidia—implying 25% upside—noting that chip demand is rapidly expanding beyond traditional hyperscalers into sovereign AI initiatives, enterprise networks, and specialized cloud developers. Microsoft received a $615 price target, a 16% gain from Tuesday's closing price. Ives pointed to the firm's expanding commercial remaining performance obligations—which reached $678 billion—as proof of broadening enterprise adoption outside of foundational frontier-model developers. Ives noted that AI systems expand security vulnerabilities faster than existing corporate IT budgets can address. Consequently, cybersecurity expenditures are projected to double, climbing from approximately 5% of overall enterprise IT spending to 10% within the next three years. As frontier labs push deeper into security architecture, cybersecurity companies are entering a prolonged growth cycle. Within this segment, Ives highlighted Palantir Technologies (PLTR) with a $250 price target (30% upside) and CrowdStrike (CRWD) with a $335 price target (20% upside). During the September 30 episode of Mad Money, Jim Cramer discussed how Microsoft Corporation's (NASDAQ:MSFT) massive artificial intelligence investment is entering a new phase as the company starts turning its data-center buildout into higher revenue. He said concerns over Azure growth, Copilot adoption, and Microsoft's relationship with OpenAI had proved misplaced. This stealth run in Microsoft has been one for the ages. Remember back in June, the stock was at $349, and many people had given up on it? We thought Azure's web services business had slowed down. We were concerned that it was too tied up with OpenAI, causing confusion about what business belonged to whom and how Microsoft is really doing. Most important, we kept hearing that customers weren't willing to pay for Microsoft's Copilot... All of these worries turned out to be either wrong or false, which is why the stock now sits at $513 with a $3.8 trillion valuation. Microsoft's accelerating AI monetization is also why it earned a place among our Top 10 AI Stocks That Will Skyrocket. But with billions still flowing into AI infrastructure, investors should also consider whether Microsoft can keep growing its dividend through the AI spending cycle. Cramer mentioned that Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is moving from a period of heavy AI infrastructure spending toward one in which those investments can generate more revenue. He said: Copilot has 30 million users and growing. They're paying as Azure's accelerating, not contracting. Microsoft seems to be separating from… gang at OpenAI... But the most important story, the biggest change, has come from something that hardly anyone talks about. Microsoft's beginning to recoup its monster data center investment. Those of us who were so troubled by the destruction of its balance sheet now realize that the data center spending might be even peaking, and profitability is beckoning. You know I'm a big believer in NVIDIA's Jensen Huang. He told me several years ago that there could be a gigantic payback on his semiconductors just a few years after they were purchased. I think Microsoft has now reached that payback period. Recently, Cramer also praised the company for its deal with Chevron. You can read about it here. In its fiscal fourth quarter, Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 27% to $59.3 billion, while Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43%. Microsoft said, "Customer demand continues to exceed available capacity." Commercial remaining performance obligations rose 84% to $678 billion, including a 25% increase excluding OpenAI. CFO Amy Hood said on September 9 that Microsoft had reduced "dock-to-live" times for infrastructure by more than 50% over the year. She said the company was focused on reducing the time between bringing infrastructure online and making it revenue-ready. Microsoft's infrastructure spending remains substantial, with capital expenditures reaching $41 billion in the June quarter. Cramer said: There's been a ton of skepticism about how the tech titans were spending insane amounts of money to build these data centers, still are. But it turns out Microsoft had to build them because there are so many customers that are clamoring for them. We stuck with Microsoft for the Charitable Trust the whole way down. Why? Because the one thing I never lost faith in was quite simple: the belief that CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood understood the data center opportunity. Cramer called the stock's post-earnings surge a "nice surprise," and you can read about it here. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) traded at 25.13x forward earnings as of September 22, according to Yahoo Finance, above Alphabet at 22.83x and Amazon at 23.64x, carrying a higher forward earnings multiple than those two large technology peers. It generated $19.6 billion of free cash flow while recording $35.8 billion of cash paid for property and equipment in the quarter. The company expects fiscal 2027 capital expenditures to increase year over year, with first-quarter spending expected to exceed $50 billion. The scale of that spending leaves it exposed if AI demand grows more slowly than expected or if new capacity takes longer to convert into revenue. Management has said spending is tied to demand and that faster deployment and infrastructure efficiencies can improve the economics of the buildout. title: MSFT Stock Nears All-Time High: Xbox Moves To Secure Exclusive Rights To Stream Grand Theft Auto VI, Report Says - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) is preparing to secure exclusive game-streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI at launch, making Xbox Cloud Gaming the only cloud service that can stream Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated title, The Verge reported Wednesday, citing sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reportedly disclosed the plan during an employee all-hands meeting, teasing that Microsoft was preparing to do something around GTA VI that “no other platform holder is doing,” according to the report. The deal would give Xbox Cloud Gaming exclusive streaming rights when the game launches, though the agreement's duration remains unclear. If the plan materializes, it would give Microsoft a significant opening beyond its console base. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.-owned (TTWO) Rockstar has yet to announce a PC version of GTA VI, meaning PC players without an Xbox Series X/S or PlayStation 5 could potentially access the game through Xbox Cloud Gaming instead, The Verge reported. MSFT stock rose 0.2% in overnight trading late Tuesday, after closing in the green for three straight sessions. It’s now less than 4% away from its record intraday high of $550.01, which it reached in July 2025, per Koyfin data. Take-Two Interactive stock rose 0.2% overnight after slipping 0.5% during regular trading. Microsoft is preparing to change how Xbox Cloud Gaming works in November, the same month GTA VI is scheduled to launch. Beginning then, Game Pass Ultimate subscribers will receive 15 hours of streaming time, while Premium and Essential subscribers will get 10 hours and five hours, respectively, according to The Verge. Microsoft is also introducing a pay-as-you-go option for Xbox Cloud Gaming, letting users buy streaming hours without subscribing to Game Pass. GTA VI is scheduled for release on Nov. 19 and is already one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in years. The sequel comes more than a decade after GTA V, which became a cultural phenomenon and one of the best-selling video games ever. The reported streaming deal comes as Xbox undergoes a broader strategic reset. In July, Microsoft announced cutting some 3,200 jobs in the Xbox division, about a fifth of the unit, and plans to sell or spin off five of its gaming studios. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for MSFT shifted to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ the previous day. “$QQQ $META $MSFT $AAPL pushing up now,” a trader remarked. The retail sentiment for TTWO was ‘bearish.’ The Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) and Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) closed at all-time high levels on Tuesday. MSFT surged nearly 38% from July through September, marking its best quarterly performance since 1998 and the strongest gain among the Magnificent Seven during the period. Marvell Technology MRVL is partnering with NVIDIA NVDA on multiple fronts, including advanced networking, optical technologies like silicon photonics and advanced optical interconnect solutions. Both companies are bringing their capabilities together. MRVL has established capabilities in optical DSPs, silicon photonics and high-speed connectivity, and NVIDIA has NVLink Fusion. Marvell Technology and NVIDIA started their initial 2025 collaboration to give hyperscalers greater flexibility in developing custom AI computing infrastructure while allowing them to leverage NVIDIA's broader rack-scale architecture, networking and software ecosystem. In 2026, the partnership was expanded, connecting MRVL to NVIDIA's AI factory and AI-RAN ecosystems through NVLink Fusion. Under the expanded arrangement, Marvell Technology will provide custom XPUs and NVLink Fusion-compatible scale-up networking, while NVIDIA will provide supporting technologies including Vera CPUs, ConnectX NICs, BlueField DPUs, NVLink interconnects, Spectrum-X switches and rack-scale AI compute. NVIDIA has further demonstrated its strategic commitment to the relationship by investing $2 billion in MRVL as part of the March 2026 partnership. The investment accompanies the expanded NVLink Fusion collaboration and reinforces Marvell Technology's role within NVIDIA's broader AI infrastructure ecosystem. Overall, the collaboration positions Marvell Technology as a key technology partner for customers seeking customized AI infrastructure while remaining connected to NVIDIA's ecosystem. MRVL also collaborated with Microsoft MSFT, and Utimaco launched Azure Payment HSM v2, a cloud-native payment security platform combining Marvell Technology's LiquidSecurity hardware security modules. Utimaco is bringing in Atalla Payments Module software, and Microsoft is offering Azure in the collaboration. The service enables banks and payment providers to secure transactions, protect cryptographic keys and meet stringent PCI compliance requirements without managing physical infrastructure. MRVL is using its hardware in multiple use cases and making it meaningful with other technology giants like NVIDIA and Microsoft. Marvell Technology competes with Astera Labs ALAB and Broadcom AVGO in the networking space. Astera Labs is benefiting from rising demand for PCIe 6 signal conditioning and AI fabric switching as hyperscalers expand rack-scale AI deployments, while Broadcom gains from traction in custom XPUs and AI networking, and VMware continues to support infrastructure software growth. Broadcom isn't collaborating with a single large partner. Broadcom has many integration partners for its VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 with integrated AI infrastructure from AMD, Intel and NVIDIA. The platform supports NVIDIA ConnectX-7 and BlueField-3 networking, while CrowdStrike enhances security and Arista Networks provides networking interoperability. Unlike Broadcom's broader integration approach and Astera Labs' connectivity focus, Marvell Technology can leverage NVIDIA's ecosystem to help hyperscalers build customized AI infrastructure while maintaining compatibility with NVIDIA's rack-scale architecture. NVIDIA's $2 billion investment further strengthens this relationship, potentially improving MRVL's access to AI infrastructure opportunities and positioning it to compete more effectively with Broadcom and Astera Labs.
